text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Friday, prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Parliament on Thursday ratified the licence agreement between Latvia and oil companies AMOCO/OPAB.

- Latvian Ministry of Defence issued a statement saying on October 23 several Russian warships including a Foxtrot-type submarine crossed Latvia's economic zone, supposedly on the way to the Russian navy base of Baltijsk. The Russian navy manoeuvres have been supervised by two Swedish Viggen aircraft.
- The presidents of Latvia and Estonia visited the former location of the Russian radar station near Skrunda and planted two trees there.

- Parliament has unanimously passed the Agriculture bill which will regulate agricultural policy in Latvia. It envisages that three percent of state budget revenues will be used to subsidise the agricultural sector.

- Prime Minister Andris Shkele met with the chairman of the Democratic Party Saimnieks and the former Deputy Prime Minister, Ziedonis Chevers, to discuss further relations between the party and the head of the government.

- Activists of the Latvian Environment Club held a picket near parliament to protest against plans by Latvia and Lithuania to intensify their oil business in the Baltic Sea by building an oil terminal at Butinge and concluding an oil exploration agreement with AMOCO/OPAB.
- In January-July 1996 black oil and gasoline have been leaders of Latvia's imports with a value of more than 30.6 million lats.
